case.title: Barrister Mohammed Kudu Nadodi and 75 Others v. Honourable Minister Federal Capital Territory and 2 Others

procedural_history.originating_proceedings: Complaint filed on 4th June 2013 by the claimants against the defendants challenging their retirement from the public service of the Federal Capital Territory.
procedural_history.procedural_posture: Notice of preliminary objection dated 29th October 2013 filed by the defendants/applicants seeking to dismiss the suit on grounds of prematurity, statute bar, and lack of jurisdiction.
interlocutory_applications: Notice of preliminary objection dated 29th October 2013
procedural_events: Claimants withdrew earlier suit instituted in 2004
Claimants filed counter affidavit and written address in opposition to the preliminary objection

material_facts: Claimants were retired from the public service of the Federal Capital Territory at various times between 2004 and 2006.
Claimants collected their severance and disengagement benefits after retirement.
A letter dated 13th June 2007 with reference FCTA/E and T/I/S. 233 reinstated 65 disengaged staff, excluding the claimants.
Claimants filed suit on 13th June 2013 challenging their retirement and seeking reinstatement and payment of arrears.

chronology.event: Claimants retired from public service of the Federal Capital Territory.
Letter reinstating 65 disengaged staff issued, excluding claimants.
Claimants filed complaint at the National Industrial Court.
Defendants filed notice of preliminary objection.

disputed_facts: Whether the retirement was irregular, illegal, and unlawful.
Whether the exclusion from reinstatement constitutes discrimination.
Whether the cause of action arose on 13th June 2007 or at the date of retirement.
background_facts: Claimants were public servants in the Federal Capital Territory.
Defendants are public officers and public bodies.
facts.employment_relationship: Contract of employment between the claimants and the defendants (Federal Capital Territory public service).
documentary_evidence: Letter of retirement issued to claimants.
Letter dated 13th June 2007 with reference FCTA/E and T/I/S. 233 reinstating 65 staff.

causes_of_action: Irregular, illegal, and unlawful retirement from public service.
Discriminatory reinstatement of 65 staff excluding claimants.
Failure to reinstate claimants and pay arrears.

claims.claim: Declaration that the retirement of the claimants is irregular, mala fide, illegal, and unlawful.
claims.legal_basis: Letter of retirement negates the intent of the FCT Staff Right Sizing letter dated 5th October 2005.

claims.claim: Declaration that the decision to reinstate 65 disengaged staff excluding the claimants is discriminatory and violates fundamental human rights.
claims.legal_basis: Section 42 of the 1999 Constitution of Nigeria (as amended) and Articles 2, 12, 19 of the African Charter on Human and Peoples' Rights.

claims.claim: Order of mandatory injunction compelling defendants to reinstate all claimants to their official positions.
Order compelling defendants to pay all salaries, arrears of rents, allowances due from date of retirement until reinstatement.

reliefs_sought.relief: Declaration that the retirement of the claimants is irregular, mala fide, illegal, and unlawful.
Declaration that the decision to reinstate 65 disengaged staff excluding the claimants is discriminatory and violates fundamental human rights.
Order of mandatory injunction compelling defendants to reinstate all claimants.
Order compelling defendants to pay salaries, arrears of rents, allowances from date of retirement until reinstatement.

issues_for_determination.issue: Whether the Public Officers Protection Act Cap P.41 LFN 2004 is applicable to this suit as presently constituted by the claimant/respondent being contractual in nature and labour related.

Whether the cause of action in this suit had arisen by virtue of the document referenced: FCTA/E and T/I/S. 233 dated 13th June 2007 titled Re: Review of Appeals of disengaged staff on the 13th day of June 2007?
Whether this Honourable court is competent to assume jurisdiction over this suit?
Whether the non filing of a memorandum of appearance by the defendant/applicant in this suit is fatal to the hearing of this notice of preliminary objection?

Whether the 5 paragraph affidavit of Joshua Achor, in support of the notice of preliminary objection dated 6th day of July 2013 but filed on the 6th day of August 2013 is not offensive to the provision of section 115 (4) of the evidence Act.

questions_of_law: Applicability of the Public Officers Protection Act to employment contracts.
Computation of limitation period for actions against public officers.
Whether failure to file memorandum of appearance precludes raising preliminary objection.

claimant_arguments: The Public Officers Protection Act is inapplicable to this case because the claim is labour-related and contractual in nature.
The cause of action arose on 13th June 2007 when the discriminatory letter was issued, and the suit filed on 13th June 2013 is within the six-year limitation period for contracts.
The court has jurisdiction as the suit is labour-related and initiated by due process.
The failure of the defendant to file a memorandum of appearance deprives them of standing to raise a preliminary objection.
The affidavit in support of the preliminary objection is offensive to section 115(4) of the Evidence Act 2011 as it contains hearsay.
defendant_arguments: The action is premature and incomplete as leave of court was not sought before filing.
The action is statute barred as it was filed more than three months after the cause of action arose, contrary to section 2(a) of the Public Officers Protection Act.
The court lacks jurisdiction due to non-compliance with the enabling statute.
The claimants admitted that the cause of action accrued between 2004 and 2007, and they collected their retirement benefits.
The continuous injury exception does not apply as the contract of employment was terminated and benefits collected.

judicial_analysis.reasoning: The court held that the defendants are public officers within the meaning of the Public Officers Protection Act. The cause of action arose between 2004 and 2006 when the claimants were retired. The suit was filed on 4th June 2013, more than three months after the accrual of the cause of action. The court rejected the argument that the Public Officers Protection Act does not apply to employment contracts, distinguishing commercial contracts. The court also held that the continuous injury exception does not apply because the employment relationship had ended and benefits were collected. The court found that the suit is statute barred and dismissed it.

issue_analysis.issue: Whether the Public Officers Protection Act Cap P.41 LFN 2004 is applicable to this suit.

arguments.claimant: The Act is inapplicable because the claim is labour-related and contractual.
arguments.defendant: The Act applies as the defendants are public officers and the acts complained of were done in the course of public duty.

issue_analysis.judicial_analysis: The court held that the Act applies to public officers and public bodies. The defendants are public officers. The act complained of (retirement) was done in the course of official duty. The Act is a statute of limitation.
issue_analysis.holding: The Public Officers Protection Act is applicable to this suit.
issue_analysis.ratio_decidendi: The Public Officers Protection Act applies to actions against public officers for acts done in the execution of public duty, including employment-related actions, unless the action falls within an exception such as continuous injury.

issue_analysis.issue: Whether the cause of action arose on 13th June 2007 or at the date of retirement.

arguments.claimant: Cause of action arose on 13th June 2007 when the discriminatory letter was issued.
arguments.defendant: Cause of action arose between 2004 and 2006 when claimants were retired.

issue_analysis.judicial_analysis: The court found that the cause of action accrued when the claimants were given letters of retirement between 2004 and 2006. The letter of 13th June 2007 was not the act complained of but a subsequent event.
issue_analysis.holding: Cause of action accrued between 2004 and 2006.
issue_analysis.ratio_decidendi: Time begins to run when all facts material to prove the claimant's case have happened, which in this case was the date of retirement.
issue_analysis.result: Cause of action accrued at retirement.

issue_analysis.issue: Whether the suit is statute barred.

arguments.claimant: The suit is not statute barred as it was filed within six years of the cause of action.
arguments.defendant: The suit is statute barred as it was filed more than three months after the cause of action.

issue_analysis.judicial_analysis: The court held that the suit was filed on 4th June 2013, more than three months after the cause of action arose between 2004 and 2006. The Public Officers Protection Act prescribes a three-month limitation period. The suit is therefore statute barred.
issue_analysis.ratio_decidendi: An action against a public officer for an act done in the execution of public duty must be commenced within three months next after the act, neglect, or default complained of, unless there is a continuance of damage or injury.

issue_analysis.issue: Whether failure to file memorandum of appearance precludes raising preliminary objection.

arguments.claimant: Failure to file memorandum of appearance deprives the defendant of standing to raise preliminary objection.
arguments.defendant: Issues of jurisdiction can be raised at any time.

issue_analysis.judicial_analysis: The court held that issues of jurisdiction can be raised at any time, even without filing a memorandum of appearance.
issue_analysis.holding: Failure to file memorandum of appearance does not preclude raising objection on jurisdiction.
issue_analysis.ratio_decidendi: Jurisdiction is fundamental and can be raised at any stage of proceedings.

issue_analysis.issue: Whether the affidavit in support of the preliminary objection is offensive to section 115(4) of the Evidence Act.

arguments.claimant: The affidavit contains hearsay and is offensive to section 115(4).

issue_analysis.judicial_analysis: The court did not make a specific finding on this issue as it was subsumed by the finding on jurisdiction.

holdings.issue: Applicability of Public Officers Protection Act
holdings.holding: The Act applies to the defendants and the acts complained of.
Cause of action accrued between 2004 and 2006.

ratio_decidendi.issue: Applicability of Public Officers Protection Act
ratio_decidendi.principle: The Public Officers Protection Act applies to actions against public officers for acts done in the execution of public duty, including employment-related actions.
ratio_decidendi.application: The defendants are public officers and the retirement of the claimants was an act done in the execution of public duty.

ratio_decidendi.principle: An action against a public officer must be commenced within three months of the act complained of, unless there is a continuance of damage or injury.
ratio_decidendi.application: The claimants were retired between 2004 and 2006 but filed suit in 2013, more than three months later. No continuous injury was established.

obiter_dicta.statement: The court called for the urgent review of the Public Officers Protection Law, describing it as a colonial legislation that should have no place in modern statute books.
obiter_dicta.context: The court's remarks on the need for law reform.
obiter_dicta.relevance: Obiter observation on the desirability of legislative reform.

legal_principles.principle: Jurisdiction is determined by the claimant's claim.
legal_principles.context: The court must look at the originating processes to determine jurisdiction.
legal_principles.source: P & C.H.S Co. Ltd v. Migfo Nig Ltd (2013) 3 NWLR (Pt 1333) at 555.

legal_principles.principle: The Public Officers Protection Act is a statute of limitation.
legal_principles.context: Actions against public officers must be filed within three months.
legal_principles.source: A.G. Rivers State v. A.G. Bayelsa State (2013) 3 NWLR Pt. 1340 123 at 148-150.

statutory_interpretation.statute: Public Officers Protection Act Cap P.41 LFN 2004
statutory_interpretation.interpretation: The Act applies to public officers and public bodies. Actions must be commenced within three months of the act complained of, unless there is a continuance of damage or injury.
statutory_interpretation.application: The defendants are public officers. The claimants were retired between 2004 and 2006. The suit filed in 2013 is statute barred.

statutory_interpretation.interpretation: Judicial review procedures require no leave of court.
statutory_interpretation.application: The claimants' suit is not a judicial review application, so leave is not required.

statutory_interpretation.interpretation: An application for judicial review shall be brought within three months and no leave is required.
statutory_interpretation.application: The claimants' suit is not a judicial review application.

constitutional_analysis.provision: Section 42 of the 1999 Constitution of Nigeria (as amended)
constitutional_analysis.application: Claimants alleged discrimination in reinstatement, but the suit was dismissed on statute bar without reaching the merits.

precedent_analysis.authority: Federal Government of Nigeria v. Zebra Energy Ltd
precedent_analysis.proposition: Public Officers Protection Act does not apply to commercial contracts.
precedent_analysis.reasoning: The court distinguished this case as it involved commercial contracts, not employment contracts.

precedent_analysis.authority: Udo v. C.S.C. Akwa Ibom State and others
precedent_analysis.proposition: For section 2(a) of the Public Officers Protection Act to avail a person, two conditions must be satisfied: the person must be a public officer, and the act must be done in pursuance of public duty.
precedent_analysis.reasoning: The court applied this test to hold that the defendants are public officers and the act was done in the course of public duty.

precedent_analysis.authority: A.G. Rivers State v. A.G. Bayelsa State
precedent_analysis.proposition: The Public Officers Protection Act is a statute of limitation; any action instituted after the prescribed period is totally barred.
precedent_analysis.reasoning: The court applied this principle to hold that the suit is statute barred.

judicial_observations: The court noted that the claimants withdrew their earlier suit in 2004 and returned after nine years, which was unfortunate.
The court called for the review of the Public Officers Protection Act.
